Q1.why: A decoder is software run over recorded chip data. It is relevant to operating qubits. Nothing physical was made.

Q2.why: As Q1: real-time decoding on TPUs, tested on recorded Willow data.

Q3.why: The circuits ran on Willow. The AI produced the circuit designs; the processor itself was not changed.

Q4.why: Encodings evaluated in simulation. Relevant to qubits, but nothing was built or run.

Q5.why: Experiment designs checked by simulated fidelity, for photonic states. The model is a task-trained transformer, so calling it autocorrect++ is a stretch.

X1.why: A change to a standards process. Nothing physical.

M1.why: Compounds were synthesized from GNoME targets. Whether AI was necessary is disputed: Cheetham & Seshadri found mostly compositional variants that a conventional screen could reach.

M2.why: A real electrolyte in a prototype cell. AI did the first screen of 32 million candidates and HPC filtering and chemists did the rest, so whether AI was necessary is arguable.

M3.why: A diffusion model designed the structure for a target property, and it was synthesized. It is one compound, so Eric rates it an early sign.

M4.why: A circuit proposed by AI is in a production TPU. Eric rates a circuit change as an early sign. The force-field and lithography gains are software speedups.

M5.why: The AI proposer chose each cycle's compositions, and 2,942 catalysts were made and tested. Of the items here it is the nearest to James's skyscraper example. It is a lab result, compared only against films made on the same platform.

M6.why: An LLM wrote the synthesis recipes and three unreported compounds were made. Whether AI was necessary is arguable: DFT screening chose the targets, people ran every step and fed results back, and the paper's claim is that fewer trials were needed.

P1.why: A learned controller held real plasma in shapes this tokamak had not produced before. That is control engineering, which James's test covers along with materials.

P2.why: Deployed and used forecasts. Eric does not count prediction as physical engineering.

P3.why: New physics about matter, confirmed by experiment. Eric counts it as knowledge; James's test asks for a leap in engineering.

P6.why: Theory. James answered this result with "I rest my case!"

P7.why: A record computation in a toy model.

P8.why: Mathematics about an equation of physics. It says nothing about real fluids.
